newsitem.title: THAILAND: FOCUS-Thai PM reshuffles cabinet to boost image.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Thai PM reshuffles cabinet to boost image.

text.p: Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh on Friday brought in a respected conservative economist and a business tycoon turned politician into his cabinet to try to improve the sagging image of his government.

Chavalit announced a cabinet reshuffle within his six-party coalition that included the appointment of former finance minister Virabongsa Ramangkura as deputy prime minister in charge of finance and fiscal affairs.
Some analysts expressed disappointment at the reshuffle, saying it fell short of market expectations.

"It's like peeling off just the outer skin of the apple without cutting into the core of the problem. I don't think it will add much value to the existing line-up although it may help a little in term of intellectual capability of handling economic problems," said Barry Yates of Seamico Securities Plc.
The Thai economy is projected to grow about 2.5-3.0 percent this year, its slowest since at least the early 1960s. Last year it grew 6.4 percent.

In the past week Chavalit has faced calls from the press, academics and the public for his resignation after a government decision to raise value added tax (VAT) to 10 percent from seven from August 16.

His government has also been criticised for suspending more than half of Thailand's 91 finance companies as the country adopted tough economic reforms in exchange for an international bail-out package worth $17 billion, according to the Thai authorities.
Virabongsa, 54, had earlier been among economists calling on the government to devalue the baht in order to halt Thailand's capital outflows and restore foreign confidence in its battered economy.

His proposal was heeded by the government which announced a de facto devaluation of the baht on July 2. The currency has since depreciated about 20 percent, forcing Thailand to seek financial assistance from the IMF.

"It should help lift the government's image and boost public confidence. Virabongsa is a technician who should get a fair degree of independence to do his job," said Sukhum Nualskul, political science professor at Ramkhamhaeng University.
Virabongsa was the architect of Thailand's decision to devalue the baht in 1984 when he played a role in managing two structural adjustment loans that Thailand obtained from the IMF.
Chavalit also named Thaksin Shinawatra, former foreign minister and owner of the Shinawatra communications group, as a deputy premier supervising trade and economic policies.

Thaksin made a political comeback after the Palang Dharma Party that he led suffered a major election defeat last November, when the party won only one seat in the 393-member House of Representatives.
Thaksin will work with Commerce Minister Narongchai Akrasanee to rein in inflation after the baht devaluation and Thailand's decision to raise the VAT.

Chavalit dropped controversial Sukavit Rangsitphol from the education portfolio. He and Deputy Interior Minister Chalerm Yoobamrung were two likely main targets of a no-confidence motion that the opposition planned to submit to parliament soon.

Sukavit had been accused by the opposition of possible corruption in his plan to equip rural government schools with computers. He had also been in acrimonious conflict with senior Thai Olympic officials organising the Bangkok Asian Games in December 1998.
Sukavit, who denied the corruption charge, retained his concurrent job as deputy premier. He is a senior member of Chavalit's New Aspiration Party.
